info.name: Bug Bounty & Disclosure Platform
info.description: End-to-end walkthrough of the API: register, create and fund a program, submit and triage a report, and pay it out. Import docs/postman_environment.json alongside this collection and select it before running. Run folders top to bottom, or use Collection Runner on the whole collection — it is idempotent (Ban/Unban User at the end resets state, and Register generates a fresh email each run). One manual step: in the Payments folder, open checkoutUrl in a browser and pay with 4242 4242 4242 4242 before running Payouts, or the reward fails with 409 INSUFFICIENT_POOL because the pool has not been funded yet.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Registration, login, and token lifecycle. Run Register first to seed accessToken/refreshToken/userId for the rest of the collection.

request.description: Creates a fresh researcher account. Generates a unique email each run.
Logs in the seeded admin account. Override the password if SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD was set to something else.
Logs in the seeded program owner account.
Needs a real Google ID token signed for GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID; a placeholder returns 401, which this request expects.
Each refresh token works once, so this replaces accessToken and refreshToken with a new pair.
Revokes the refresh token. Placed last in this folder so earlier requests in a full run still have a live token; run it on its own to actually log out.

item.name: Programs
item.description: Bug bounty programs and their reward tiers. Requests use the seeded program owner.

request.description: A program needs at least one reward tier before it can go ACTIVE.

item.name: Payments
item.description: Stripe checkout and pool funding. The webhook is called by Stripe, not from Postman; use Verify Payment or the Stripe CLI (`stripe trigger checkout.session.completed`) instead.

request.description: Returns a hosted Stripe URL. Open data.checkoutUrl in a browser and pay with card 4242 4242 4242 4242 to complete it for real.

Asks Stripe directly for the session status and applies it. Run this after paying through checkoutUrl in a browser, to credit the pool without waiting on the webhook. A no-op until the checkout is actually completed.

Called by Stripe, not from Postman — it needs a valid Stripe-Signature header over the raw body, which Postman cannot produce. Stripe calls this automatically once `stripe listen --forward-to localhost:5000/api/v1/payments/webhook` is running. Sending it from here without a signature returns 400, which this request expects.

item.name: Reports
item.description: Vulnerability reports and triage. Submission uses the fresh researcher account; triage uses the seeded admin. Run the Payments folder first so the pool can afford the reward in the Payouts folder.

request.description: Only legal while the report is NEW or NEEDS_INFO.
The program must already have a reward tier for the chosen severity.

item.name: Comments
item.description: Discussion thread on a report. Open to anyone who can see the report.

item.name: Payouts
item.description: Rewards paid to researchers. Reward Report is the concurrency-safe money-moving endpoint (see README).

request.description: Debits the program pool, credits the researcher's wallet and reputation, and marks the report REWARDED. Run it twice to see 409 ALREADY_REWARDED.

item.name: Admin
item.description: User management, audit log, and platform stats. Admin only.

request.description: Promotes the demo researcher created by Register. Refused on your own account and on the last active admin.
Pauses the user's ACTIVE programs if they own any.
Undoes the previous request, so re-running this collection from the top still works.

item.name: Cleanup (optional)
item.description: Soft-delete requests. Not part of the automated run — both are expected to return 409 against the demo data left by the rest of this collection (the program's pool is not empty, and REWARDED is not a withdrawable report status), which is correct, documented behavior, not a bug. Run them by hand against a program/report with no funds or open work to see the 200 path.
